title: Playdate for Two
teaser: Your puppy has made plans, and you are invited.
clue: Someone small has sent an invitation and chosen the menu. You are on the guest list.
reveal: A short, floor-level playdate with a menu of three gentle games, a nap course in between, and a puppy who picks the favorite by simply coming back for more.
objective: Share a short floor-level playdate where your puppy picks from three gentle games and you both rest in between.
instructions: Pick a clear room and sit on the floor with a blanket. Lay out the 'menu': a towel, a soft puppy-safe tug toy and a soft ball bigger than your puppy's mouth.
Course one, Peekaboo: drape the towel over your knee to make a tent, lift one corner and say your puppy's name softly. Let them poke, pounce or leave.
Course two, Soft Snake: slide the tug toy slowly along the floor, like a snake that is easy to catch. Let your puppy win it often, keep any tug gentle and brief, and stay beside them the whole time.
Course three, Rolling Ball: roll the ball a short way across the floor. Watch for which game your puppy comes back to; that is the winner.
After two minutes of any game, call a nap course. Sit quietly with the blanket while your puppy rests, sniffs or chews a toy that suits their age.
Finish with a gentle chat and a cuddle if your puppy wants one, then tidy the tug toy and ball out of reach.
twist: Your puppy is the host: the three games are a menu, the favorite is whichever they return to, and a nap is built into every playdate.
variations: Seated version: play from a chair with the games rolled across a short stretch of floor.
Only the towel tent, for puppies who prefer calm games.
No tug toy? Use a large soft toy that is too big to swallow, and supervise closely.
Skip the ball if your puppy is more interested in cuddling.
completion: You have played at least one game that your puppy joined in, and you have had a rest together.
photoIdea: The menu on the floor with your puppy's favorite game lined up in front of it.
memoryPrompt: Which game did your puppy keep returning to, and what did their rest look like?
supplies: Soft ball bigger than your puppy's mouth
substitutes: No puppy-safe tug toy? A large soft toy.
No soft ball? A large, soft, rolled-up towel.
safety: Home only until your vet says public places are fine; no strange dogs, just you two.
Supervise every moment of play, keep it short and soft, and take away any toy that gets chewed apart.
Stop for a nap at the first sign of tiredness; puppies need plenty of rest.
